title: USWNT will host Spain twice in October for World Cup qualifying preparation
content:
The U.S. women’s national team will face its next major test ahead of World Cup qualifying, hosting top-ranked Spain in a pair of friendlies in October. The U.S. will square off against Spain in Washington, D.C. on Oct. 10 before heading north to Subaru Park in Chester, Pa., on Oct. 13.

“We’ve desperately wanted to get Spain on our schedule,”  coach Emma Hayes said in a news release, “but the difficulties of scheduling the top teams during the women’s international calendar are well known, so to be able to get these two games on the East Coast will be the perfect tests before we head into World Cup qualifying at the end of the year.”

Spain qualified for the World Cup in June, breezing through European qualification, including a 4-0 romp over England and a 6-1 defeat of Iceland, freeing up their fall schedule to play the U.S. Spain directly qualified for the 2027 World Cup, while USWNT has to wait for Concacaf’s qualifying window later this year that will run through the end of November into early December.

Spain will serve as another aggressive test for the U.S. under Hayes. A pair of friendlies against Brazil in Brazil during the June window helped get the players a test of the hostile — and incredible — atmospheres that await them next summer if they qualify.

“That’s why I keep leaning into the fact that sometimes we create too many perfect conditions,” Hayes said in June.

While the home crowds in October’s friendlies against Spain will be much friendlier to the U.S., the competition will be anything but. There’s relatively little history between these two top-ranked teams, with the USWNT holding the edge in wins (three) to Spain’s one. However, Spain have had a dominant run, including winning the 2023 World Cup.

There are still plenty of questions for Hayes and the potential roster ahead of next summer’s World Cup in Brazil, from the impact of the return of the Triple Espresso line of Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson and Mal Swanson to who will be the team’s starting goalkeeper. Two friendlies against Spain should be a proving ground for players who might still be on the bubble.

Crystal Dunn, who retired in January, will be honored ahead of the first match at Audi Field. The Washington Spirit selected Dunn with the No. 1 pick in the 2014 college draft, and she had a breakout season in 2015, winning the NWSL Golden Boot and MVP award. Dunn was also a key part of the U.S. team that won the 2019 World Cup.
